topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and sets the clinical and biological scope of cancer biology.

topics.label: Cancer as a Stepwise Failure of Differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the fundamental concept of cancer as an accumulation of genetic changes leading to a failure of cellular differentiation, and examine the challenges of studying this in tissue architecture and culture.

topics.label: Invasion, Metastasis, and Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how tumors progress from benign to invasive and metastatic malignancies, using colorectal cancer as a histological model of stepwise transformation.

topics.label: Principles of Tumor Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the standardized terminology and suffix conventions used to classify benign and malignant tumors across different tissue origins.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Disease and Mortality in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the physical and systemic mechanisms by which primary tumors and secondary metastases cause clinical illness and death.

topics.label: Comparative Incidence and Cancer Across Species
topics.groupedBecause: They analyze patterns of tumor incidence and mortality across human tissues and examine how cancer affects diverse multicellular animal species.

topics.label: Cancer Detection and Population Screening
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the clinical principles of early cancer detection and compare screening strategies and outcomes across different tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Preparation
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a reminder of the learning outcomes and upcoming practical sessions.
